overview.text: The Eastern Worm Snake is a small, harmless burrowing snake of the eastern United States. It is common but rarely seen, because it lives under logs, stones and in the soil.

identification.text: Plain tan to dark brown on top with a bright pink belly; the pink reaches up onto the lowest scale rows of the sides. It has smooth scales, a pointed head and small black eyes.

size.label: Adults
size.text: A small snake; the record is 34 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The eastern United States east of the Mississippi, from southern New England and New York south to Georgia and Alabama, and west to Louisiana and Illinois.

habitat.text: Moist, rocky woodland, under rotting logs and stumps.

behaviour.text: A burrower that is seldom seen above ground, especially in summer.

recognise.text: Plain brown back and pink belly.
